candidates.topic: DIMS long-term myopia control and baseline RPR responder stratification
candidates.original_question: 離焦鏡片成效不佳，可能不是鏡片無效，而是孩子的周邊屈光型態不同嗎？
candidates.social_signal_basis: The study was surfaced through a current professional optometry news placement and its public journal page during the seven-day window; no likes, comments, shares, impressions, or other engagement metric was collected or inferred.
candidates.evidence_candidate: A public observational follow-up reports outcomes beyond eight years for prior DIMS wearers. The continuous-wear subgroup was small, and the reported 0.57 mm lower axial elongation and estimated 56% inhibition concerned a hyperopic baseline relative peripheral refraction subgroup compared with historical controls, so this is a predictor-stratification candidate rather than a product-wide effectiveness conclusion.
candidates.research_gap: Test baseline relative peripheral refraction as a pre-specified predictor of long-term axial response in a sufficiently powered prospective cohort with concurrent controls, adherence tracking, and product-history control. Keep three constructs separate: long-term DIMS effectiveness, RPR-based responder stratification, and visual-quality or adaptation outcomes from peripheral-defocus optics. Also distinguish ocular RPR in this study from the vault's non-formal mRCRP concept for post-orthokeratology relative corneal refractive power.
candidates.recommendation_reason: If the owner approves intake, extend the existing peripheral-defocus root through its mechanism and individual-difference branches. Do not reuse the existing visual-quality research question as though it measured axial efficacy or RPR-defined response.

related_existing_nodes.note: Same child peripheral-defocus domain and DIMS exposure, but KDF-001 asks whether visual-function evidence keeps pace with efficacy evidence; the pilot asks about long-term axial effectiveness and response prediction.
Baseline peripheral refractive profile is a plausible optical-mechanism branch, but this mother topic is only a skeleton and has no existing responder-prediction question.
RPR responder stratification is an individual-difference question. The mother topic is structurally appropriate but currently has no research question.

Population and DIMS exposure overlap, but the existing outcomes are central/off-axis visual quality, low-contrast performance, adaptation, and daily function. They do not cover long-term axial elongation or RPR as an effect modifier.

duplicate_risk.reason: Structured comparison found the same child population and DIMS/peripheral-defocus exposure under Root KDF-001, with a strong conceptual home in Mother KDF-001-F and a mechanism link to KDF-001-A. Comparator and outcomes differ from KDF-001-B-001: this pilot concerns historical or concurrent controls, axial elongation, long-term effectiveness, and baseline RPR effect modification, while the existing research question concerns visual quality and adaptation. The research gap is therefore adjacent but not duplicative; extending the root is safer than reusing or merging the visual-quality node.

candidates.topic: AI adoption, privacy, integration, documentation, and responsibility governance in optometry
candidates.original_question: 視光機構導入 AI 時，疾病偵測與 AI scribe／紀錄摘要的採用、資料隱私、軟體整合及責任／保險治理，應如何分層評估，而不是視為單一 AI 導入問題？
candidates.social_signal_basis: Two specialist eyecare publications surfaced related adoption and governance concerns during the same seven-day window. This is a qualitative editorial-placement signal only; no engagement count or unsupported popularity metric was collected or inferred.
candidates.evidence_candidate: One professional-media article reports vendor or industry survey observations about optometry and healthcare AI use, including limited reported disease-detection use, privacy concern, and lack of software-stack integration. A second professional-association feature uses AI call recording and summarization to outline data-processing agreements, storage location, encryption, access control, breach handling, patient notice, and insurance disclosure. These are bounded adoption and governance leads, not verified clinical-effectiveness evidence.
candidates.research_gap: Build separate verification tracks for: AI disease-detection performance and referral responsibility; AI scribe or documentation accuracy and record correction; privacy, retention, controller/processor and cross-border data duties; interoperability and duplicate-entry burden; and professional responsibility, liability, incident response, and insurance. Determine how these tracks map to Taiwan PDPA, local medical-record duties, optometrist scope, vendor contracts, and insurer requirements. Existing non-formal vault notes cover disease-detection examples, but not this cross-workflow governance question.
candidates.recommendation_reason: If the owner approves intake, create a new governance-oriented research path with explicit subquestions. Professional-media and vendor-survey claims must remain source leads and cannot become evidence without primary-source and jurisdiction-specific verification.

duplicate_risk.reason: All 18 formal KDF artifacts were compared by population, exposure, comparator, outcomes, mechanism, research gap, and Root/Mother/Research Question relationships. The formal tree concerns children wearing peripheral-defocus myopia-control lenses; this pilot concerns optometry practices using disease-detection and documentation AI, with governance outcomes around privacy, integration, accountability, liability, and insurance. Vault-wide context includes non-formal AI disease-detection paper notes, but no formal KDF ID covers AI scribe workflows, data governance, software integration, or responsibility allocation. No formal node is suitable for REUSE or EXTEND.
